title: Regionally sticky fleets: latency-aware quota fencing and soft-evacuation policy
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Implement regionally sticky dedicated pools that provide per-customer throughput guarantees while enforcing data residency constraints and enabling soft evacuation/failover with latency-aware quota fencing. This ticket captures the design, implementation plan, tests, and rollout for the policy and control plane pieces required by Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can create pool-config with region_preference, residency_hard_flag, min_throughput_qps, and soft_evacuate_window
Requests respect region_preference for placement if capacity exists and data residency rules allow
When a zone is marked draining, the system enforces soft_evacuate_window semantics: new connections are prevented after window expiry and existing sessions are drained per policy
Throughput guarantees for reserved tenants are enforced by quota fencing so noisy tenants cannot exceed reserved bandwidth on shared hosts
Failover order is deterministic and respects residency_hard_flag (no cross-region failover if hard residency) and logs audit events
Metrics (p50/p95 request latencies, tokens/sec per-tenant, failover time) are visible in Console and match targets in runbook
Migration/upgrade plan exists for existing dedicated pools with minimal customer disruption (migration < 10% request drop on average)
design_notes: Core idea: combine placement-layer region-preferences + token-level quota fencing + a control-plane soft-drain window to deliver predictable latency and throughput guarantees without rigidly preventing failover when safe

Placement policy: primary region (sticky) -> zone affinity -> fallback region list ordered by explicit policy. For each candidate, verify residency constraints via dataset tags and legal flags before routing

Quota fencing: enforce per-tenant tokens/sec and concurrent-req ceilings at the host allocator using a leaky-bucket limiter mounted in the request proxy. This prevents tail latency amplification from noisy neighbors

Soft evacuation: when drain initiated, mark host with drain_ts and a soft_evacuate_window. New requests are allowed until drain_ts+window; after that, new requests are rejected and proxy immediately starts slow-drain of KV caches and session transfer hooks

Evacuation priority: critical-residency tenants (residency_hard_flag=true) are prevented from cross-region failover; non-critical tenants are eligible and ordered by least-recently-failed region/latency impact

KV cache considerations: prefer routing to hosts with warm KV caches for a tenant where possible; during soft-evacuate, cache warms are pre-populated in target hosts using segmented prewarm (hot keys only) to reduce steady-state latency after failover

Autoscale interaction: autoscaler differentiates between planned soft-evacuations (trigger horizontal prewarm) and unplanned capacity loss (trigger emergency spillover to fallback regions). Autoscaler policies include scale-up thresholds that respect per-tenant min_throughput_qps
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Hard residency vs availability: legal/customer requirements sometimes mandate no cross-region failover. We selected a residency_hard_flag to make that explicit; default is false to preserve availability for most customers
Quota fencing location: implementing in proxy adds one hop but centralizes enforcement; alternative was host-local cgroups which would complicate cross-host coordination
Soft-evacuate window duration: default 60s chosen after load-test spike analysis balancing drain completeness vs failover speed; configurable per-pool
Prewarm scope: prewarming entire model state is costly; we limit prewarm to top-k hot KV segments, allowing acceptable latency while controlling cost
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike): build placement policy prototype in orchestrator service + unit tests and conformance checks (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Quota fencing): implement per-tenant leaky-bucket limiter in proxy and expose metrics; integrate with billing tokens-per-second counters (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (Soft-evacuate): add drain flags and soft_evacuate_window support to host lifecycle; implement session drain hooks and KV segmented prewarm (4 weeks)
Phase 4 (Autoscale integration): update autoscaler to recognize planned vs unplanned drain and prewarm targets; add experiment toggles (2 weeks)
Phase 5 (End-to-end tests + canary): run synthetic traffic sims, chaos tests (zone-eviction), and limited customer canary rollout (2 weeks)
Phase 6 (Rollout): gradual ramp across regions following rollout plan and update operator docs/runbooks (1 week)
testing_plan: Unit tests for placement decision matrix and residency flag validation
Load tests with mixed-tenant profiles to validate quota fencing under noisy neighbor scenarios
Chaos simulation: simultaneous zone drain + autoscale to validate stability and prewarm efficacy
Latency SLO verification: synthetic traffic verifies p95 latency increase remains < 15% during planned evacuations
Audit tests: verify audit logs are emitted for any cross-region routing involving residency_hard_flag=false tenants
rollout_plan: Start with internal dedicated pool in us-west1 with canary tenants (5 customers) for 2 weeks
Expand to additional pools in us-east1 and europe-west1 with staged ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) per region
Monitor Console dashboards and automated regression alerts; hold/fix if any metric breaches critical thresholds
Enable security_review_required gate before cross-region failover for Enterprise customers
Post-rollout retrospective and capture runbook improvements
metrics_and_slo_targets: p50 latency target: <= 30ms for intra-region requests
p95 latency target: <= 120ms for intra-region requests
tokens/sec guarantee: per-tenant min_throughput_qps applied with 98% adherence
noisy-neighbor leakage: tenant burst cannot exceed allocated throttle for more than 5s without backpressure
runbook_and_playbooks: Runbook: dedicated/region-evacuation.md - steps to initiate soft-evacuate and abort/force-evacuate
Playbook: failover-escalation.txt - contact SRE, enable emergency spillover, revert if >2x latency breach
Visibility: Console dashboards updated with per-tenant throughput, host drain state, and prewarm progress
